title: Affiliate Ops Reconciler
one_liner: Upload Shopify/affiliate exports and get a reconciled creator payout ledger with tiered commissions, promo-code overlap handling, suspicious attribution flags, anomalies and payment-ready totals.
buyer: DTC Shopify brands with roughly 20-100 active creators that have outgrown spreadsheets but do not want enterprise affiliate software or a dedicated marketing-ops hire.

pain.description: Monthly reconciliation of creator commissions, custom tiers, promo-code overlaps, attribution exceptions and payouts becomes manual, error-prone and financially risky as affiliate programs grow.

evidence.signal: A DTC skincare brand at about $300k/year with 35 creators says its Shopify plugin + large spreadsheet setup is becoming unmanageable and is actively evaluating affiliate-management software because reconciliation and payouts consume substantial team time.

A merchant using GoAffPro reports a creator-code/subscription-discount collision: creator commission should remain while customer discounts should not stack; the workaround described is explicitly messy.

A fast-scaling Shopify brand says it calculates affiliate and creator payouts from exports and pays partners manually one-by-one, and is actively looking for scheduled automated payouts with review/approval.

A merchant running affiliates across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube describes two parallel programs whose data does not talk to each other; Shopify native tooling is described as too limited for tiered commissions and performance bonuses.

evidence.source: Shopify App Store review of GoAffPro
evidence.signal: A merchant reports paying more than $20k in allegedly fraudulent affiliate commissions after attribution interacted badly with existing discount codes/UTMs; GoAffPro replies that merchants must review and configure attribution rules themselves. This indicates a possible audit/reconciliation wedge rather than a need to replace the affiliate platform.

product_shape.v0: CSV/XLSX in -> normalized transactions -> deterministic commission rules -> overlap/attribution exceptions -> suspicious-commission flags -> anomaly report -> creator payout ledger out.
product_shape.wedge: Audit and reconcile the output of existing affiliate systems instead of replacing them.

distribution.primary: Shopify App Store after file-based validation; the app-store listing itself is a real acquisition surface.
distribution.secondary: High-intent search around affiliate commission reconciliation, creator payout spreadsheets, coupon-code leakage and attribution overlap.
distribution.constraint: Do not treat a Railway URL as distribution. Do not publicly launch until there is an actual acquisition route.

monetization_hypotheses: $39-$99/month recurring reconciliation/audit by creator or order volume
Higher-value recovery fee only if the tool can identify demonstrably invalid commissions

validation.next_gate: competitive wedge and file-level prototype value
validation.important_uncertainty: Existing affiliate platforms may already cover enough reconciliation for most merchants; the strongest wedge may be independent audit/fraud/over-attribution detection rather than payout calculation itself.

falsification: Compare the narrow audit/reconciliation wedge against current low-cost Shopify affiliate tools. Kill if existing tools already expose equivalent overlap/fraud diagnostics simply, or if useful detection requires inaccessible attribution data rather than merchant exports.
kill: Kill or radically reframe if low-cost incumbents already solve the audit problem cleanly, if merchant exports are insufficient for useful detection, or if no credible acquisition surface exists without manual selling.
persist: Persist if merchant exports are sufficient to flag real payout/attribution anomalies and multiple existing-tool users still report costly exceptions or manual review.
scale: Only build Shopify-native integration after a file-based audit prototype proves it produces findings merchants consider worth paying for.
